project.objective: When and where did Anders Monsen marry Unna Halsteinsdatter, and what does the marriage record show?

questions.question: When and where did Anders Monsen marry Unna Halsteinsdatter, and what does the marriage record show?
questions.rationale: This is the objective restated as a single researchable question. The marriage is a single event — date and place are two attributes of one fact. Norwegian church registers (kirkebøker) routinely recorded marriage date, parish, witnesses, and parental information, making this testable from original sources. Addressing this question first establishes the spousal relationship in evidence and anchors any downstream research on the couple's family.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: goal_alignment, repository_breadth, independent_verification, evidence_class, and overturn_risk all fail. Seven plans (pl_001–pl_007), 24 plan items, and 69 log entries have exhausted every automated avenue available in this environment. All FamilySearch indexed collections for Norwegian marriages (1468080), church books (4237104), baptisms (1467014), burials (1468081), probate (1661306), and censuses (1865/1870/1875/1891/1900) were attempted with all name variants. Four fulltext_search queries returned 0 results. FamilySearch volume_search confirmed zero Voss church book image volumes on FamilySearch for 1820–1900. The 1900 census image browse (pli_021, 22 pages sampled from a 670-image volume) found neither Anders Monsen nor Unna Halsteinsdatter, consistent with both having died before 1900. Ancestry.com (pli_022) and MyHeritage (pli_023) URLs were generated but WebFetch was denied; these are subscription/fee sites. Digitalarkivet.no — Norway's national digital archive and the sole confirmed repository for the Voss kirkebok Ektevigselsbok (marriage register) series — was attempted six or more times (log_032, log_051, log_052, log_062, log_065, log_069) and blocked each time by permanent WebFetch environment policy. The inaccessibility exception does NOT apply: Digitalarkivet.no is a free, publicly accessible website reachable by any human researcher — only automated WebFetch is blocked, not the source itself. No defensible conclusion exists from accessible evidence (zero records located). An automated environment's inability to fetch a public website is not equivalent to a source sealed by privacy law or physically destroyed. The kirkebok is the gating record type (wiki-query-api server offline again on this evaluation; Norway civil registration start date unverified from wiki, but loc_001 confirms kirkebøker are the primary pre-civil-registration marriage source). Terminating as not-yet-exhaustive for the sixth time: the research is incomplete in this environment. A human researcher must: (1) browse Digitalarkivet.no — Church books → Hordaland → Voss → Ektevigselsbok → 1840–1880, searching for groom 'Anders Monsen' and bride variants 'Unna'/'Urna'/'Udna' Halsteinsdatter/Halsteinsdr; (2) check Ancestry.com Norwegian church records; (3) check MyHeritage Norwegian records.

questions.question: Who comprised the household of Halstein (father of Unna Halsteinsdatter) in Voss, Hordaland, Norway circa 1865?
questions.rationale: Priority 6 FAN pivot. All 16 planned direct searches across 4 plans are complete or skipped, all negative or timed-out (error). Digitalarkivet.no — the only repository holding the Voss kirkebok marriage registers — has been attempted three times and blocked by permanent WebFetch environment policy (log_032, log_051, log_052). FamilySearch record_search is experiencing a transient service outage (pli_013–016, log_054–057). No automated direct-evidence path remains available in this environment. This FAN question targets Halstein — identified by Unna's patronymic as her father — in the 1865 Norwegian census (col. 3756102, 1,688,075 indexed records). His household composition that year brackets the marriage of Unna to Anders Monsen: if Unna appears unmarried in Halstein's household, the marriage post-dates 1865; if she is absent, the marriage pre-dates 1865. The 1875 census is a secondary source for the same bracketing. This evidence directly informs q_001's marriage date and is the highest-value FAN path available once the FamilySearch record_search service recovers.

items.rationale: FamilySearch collection 1468080, 'Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926', contains 1,330,979 indexed records (personCount confirmed by collections_search). This is the highest-probability first item: search by groom name 'Anders Monsen' and bride name 'Unna Halsteinsdatter'. Norwegian marriage registers (kirkebøker) typically recorded date, parish, groom and bride, both fathers' names (confirming the patronymics), witnesses, and ages. Per loc_001: collection 1468080 has 0 images — once a match is found, retrieve the original image from collection 4237104 or Digitalarkivet.no. Try variant spellings: Mohnsen, Andersen (in case of early fixed-name use), Halsteindatter, Halsteins Datter.

FamilySearch collection 4237104, 'Norway, Church Books, 1797-1958', contains 14,398,439 indexed records and 1,288,153 images (collections_search). Broader than collection 1468080: includes baptisms, marriages, burials, and confirmations in one searchable corpus with original images. If the marriage entry does not surface in pli_001, search this collection directly by name. Also use this collection to retrieve the original kirkebok image after pli_001 identifies the entry (since 1468080 has no images). Searching here may also surface a baptism or confirmation for Anders Monsen that names his father Mons Monsen and anchors the family to a specific parish.

FAN item. FamilySearch holds indexed Norwegian censuses for 1865 (col. 3756102, 1,688,075 records with images), 1875 (col. 1529106, 333,541 records), and 1891 (col. 4067726, 2,727,197 records with images). Search each for Anders Monsen. A census hit will: (a) identify the specific parish (prestegjeld) where the family lived — the prerequisite for browsing unindexed kirkebok volumes (per loc_001 quirk: all records organized at parish level); (b) confirm Unna Halsteinsdatter or Unna Monsen as co-resident spouse, establishing the marriage occurred before the census year; (c) show children's ages, bracketing the approximate marriage year. As a FAN item: the household enumeration names neighbors and household members who shared the same church community, providing context for where the marriage record was filed and potentially naming relatives of both Anders and Unna.

Digitalarkivet.no (https://digitalarkivet.no/) is the Norwegian National Archives' digital repository and the authoritative source for Norwegian historical records. It holds church records (kirkebøker), civil marriage indexes (from c.1863 per external_links_search data showing sets covering 1863-1919, 1883-1919, 1887-1910, 1891-1908, 1892-1912, 1893+), emigration records, and indexes not fully mirrored on FamilySearch. Since the marriage date is unknown, search both church-era (pre-1890s) and civil-era registers. Execute via search-external-sites skill. The site is free.

Full-text co-occurrence search fallback. Per loc_001: 18,963 digitized volumes for Norway marriage/religious records exist, most at 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable (browse-only). If the indexed collections (pli_001, pli_002) fail to surface the marriage — because the specific parish's volumes are not name-indexed — run a full-text search using 'Monsen' and 'Halstein' (Unna's father's name, embedded in her patronymic 'Halsteinsdatter') as a co-occurrence across the Norwegian church book corpus via the search-full-text skill. This tactic targets AI-transcribed page text from volumes that are not name-indexed. Do not scope to a specific collection id; run unscoped across the full corpus. Also try 'Anders' + 'Unna' as a name-pair co-occurrence if the surname search yields nothing.

FamilySearch collection 4067726 (Norway, Census, 1891) has 2,727,197 indexed records and 2,454,861 images — fully searchable. The 1891 census for Voss specifically (imageGroupNumber 107236654, 7,667 images, 100% searchable) is within this collection. The 1891 census records the household head, spouse, children, and their birthplaces and ages. A hit for Anders Monsen in Voss/Hordaland would: (a) confirm Unna Halsteinsdatter/Monsen as his wife, establishing that the marriage occurred before 1891; (b) give the specific parish (prestegjeld or sokn) where the family lived — the key for then locating the unindexed kirkebok marriage volume on Digitalarkivet.no; (c) show children's birth years, bracketing when the marriage took place. Prior census searches (log_026, log_027) covered 1865 and 1875 without a place filter; the 1891 census has not been searched. Search with residencePlace: Voss, Hordaland.

FamilySearch collection 3744863 (Norway, Census, 1900) has 2,260,720 indexed records — name-searchable. The 1900 census volumes for Voss (imageGroupNumbers 107203067, 107203065, 107203066) are browse-only at the volume level, but the collection itself is indexed, so a name search for Anders Monsen with residencePlace Voss or Hordaland will surface the entry if he was alive in 1900. The 1900 census is particularly useful because log_028 found 'Unni Halsteinsdtr' born 1898 in Vossestrand — placing a younger Halsteinsdatter in the exact Voss area, corroborating that geographic lead. Search as fallback to pli_006 if 1891 yields no result.

FAN/corroboration item. FamilySearch collection 1467014 (Norway, Baptisms, 1634-1927) has 5,277,294 indexed records. Norwegian baptism entries name both parents: 'Anders Monsen og [wife's name]' plus the child's name and the officiating parish. Searching for baptisms where fatherGivenName='Anders' and fatherSurname='Monsen' (or father surname 'Mohnsen') will surface the children of Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter — each baptism record names the church parish, which identifies exactly where to find the marriage register on Digitalarkivet.no. This is the key FAN path: the children's baptism records name the parents and fix the family to a specific parish, corroborating when and where the marriage occurred even before the marriage record itself is found.

Digitalarkivet.no is Norway's national digital archive and the primary repository for Norwegian church records and civil registration. Unlike pli_004 (which searched the general person search), this item targets the marriage-register search directly: https://www.digitalarkivet.no/en/content/church-books/marriage — using parish name once identified from pli_006 or pli_008, or by browsing the Voss prestegjeld marriage registers for 1840-1880. The site is free and holds transcriptions of the Voss kirkebøker that are not name-indexed on FamilySearch. WebFetch is blocked in this environment; the researcher must browse manually. This is the highest-probability path to the actual marriage record given that FamilySearch indexed collections (pli_001–pli_005) were exhausted. URLs: https://www.digitalarkivet.no/search/marriage?place=Voss and https://register.digitalarkivet.no/kb/voss

FamilySearch collection 1661306 (Norway, Probate Index Cards, 1640-1903) has 1,058,029 indexed records. A probate record for Halstein (Unna's father) would name Unna Halsteinsdatter as a daughter and may name her husband Anders Monsen, giving the marriage date and place indirectly. Halstein (Unna's father) likely died between c.1840 and c.1920 — date window sized to the creator's lifespan. Search for surname 'Halstein' or given name 'Halstein' in the probate index, filtering to Hordaland/Voss area. Also search for Anders Monsen probate if he died before 1903, which would name Unna as widow.

Digitalarkivet.no holds the digitized Voss kirkebok (church book) series including Ektevigselsbok (marriage registers). FamilySearch volume_search confirmed zero browse-only church book image volumes for Voss in 1820–1900, so this is the only remaining repository that may hold Voss marriage records. The Voss (Vossestrand / Vossevangen) marriage registers for this period are browsable at https://www.digitalarkivet.no/en/content/church-books/. WebFetch is blocked in the current automated environment; if unreachable, this item will be logged as inaccessible and the plan closed per BCG Standard 18. The researcher should browse: Digitalarkivet → Church books → Hordaland → Voss → Marriage (Ektevigselsbok) → 1820–1900, searching for Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter.

If any Voss kirkebok pages have been transcribed (even without name indexing), a co-occurrence search for 'Anders' and 'Halsteinsdatter' or 'Monsen' may surface the marriage entry. Primary path. The 1865 Norwegian census (1,688,075 indexed records) is the most direct source for Halstein's household composition. BCG Std 11: Halstein is identified only by his role as Unna Halsteinsdatter's father (stated by her patronymic); his own patronymic surname is unknown. Two complementary search angles: (1) givenName='Halstein' + recordCountry='Norway' + residencePlace='Voss, Hordaland' — finds him as head of household; (2) surname='Halsteinsdatter' + recordCountry='Norway' + residencePlace='Voss, Hordaland' — finds daughters listed in his household. loc_001 quirk: patronymic naming means surname changed each generation, so given-name anchoring is the correct strategy when surname is unknown. Also try variant 'Hallstein'. A hit showing Unna Halsteinsdatter as an unmarried daughter confirms she married Anders Monsen after 1865; her absence suggests the marriage predates 1865.

5,277,294 indexed records. Search by fatherGivenName='Halstein' with residencePlace='Voss, Hordaland, Norway'. Norwegian baptism entries name both parents with their given names and patronymics. A hit names Unna (or her siblings) as Halstein's children, directly confirming Halstein's parentage of Unna and identifying the specific Voss parish where the family lived. Date window sized to the creator's plausible birth range (1840–1880): Unna was likely born circa 1840–1860 given she was of marrying age circa 1865–1875; Halstein's children would have been baptized in that window. Also try fatherGivenName='Hallstein' as a variant. A sibling's baptism naming fatherGivenName='Halstein' and a residence in Voss is the strongest corroboration of Unna's parentage without the marriage register itself.

Fallback for pli_017 if 1865 census yields no result, and complementary bracketing source if 1865 shows Unna still unmarried. 333,541 indexed records. Same dual search strategy: givenName='Halstein' for head of household, and surname='Halsteinsdatter' for daughters in the household. If Unna was in Halstein's household in 1865 (unmarried) but gone by 1875, the marriage is bracketed to 1865–1875. If she's also present in 1875 (still unmarried), the marriage post-dates 1875.

719,685 indexed records. Halstein's burial record may name his surviving children including Unna and her married name (Unna Monsen), providing indirect evidence that she married Anders Monsen. Search by givenName='Halstein' + recordCountry='Norway' + residencePlace='Voss, Hordaland'. Date window sized to Halstein's plausible lifespan: if Unna was born circa 1840–1860, Halstein likely lived from circa 1810–1900, making the burial range 1820–1903 (the collection's end date). Also try 'Hallstein'. A burial record naming a daughter's husband is the strongest indirect evidence of the marriage and may supply the specific parish for the kirkebok search at Digitalarkivet.no.

quirks: All vital records are organized at the parish (prestegjeld) level — identify the parish before browsing the 18,000+ digitized volumes; use the indexed marriage collection (1468080) to find the entry and thereby identify the parish.
Patronymic naming: men took -sen (son of father's first name), women took -datter; surnames changed each generation. Search on first name + approximate year when surname variants yield no results.

Church records (kirkebøker) are the primary marriage source for the entire pre-civil registration period (~pre-1890s). Civil marriage indexes on Digitalarkivet.no begin c.1863 and broaden in the 1880s-1890s.
Norway, Marriages 1660-1926 (collection 1468080) has 1.3 million indexed records but ZERO images — retrieve images from Norway, Church Books 1797-1958 (collection 4237104) or Digitalarkivet.no.

Most parish-level kirkebok volumes on FamilySearch are 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — browse-only. Identifying the parish from an indexed collection entry is the prerequisite to image-browsing.

Digitalarkivet.no (https://digitalarkivet.no/) is the Norwegian national digital archive and should be searched in parallel with FamilySearch — it holds civil marriage records, emigration records, and additional church record scans.
Records are in Norwegian / Dano-Norwegian; marriage entries use standard formulaic terminology. Key fields: dato (date), navn (name), foreldre (parents).
The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Norway were unavailable at time of survey (wiki-query-api server offline); consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway when the server is restored.
Population statistics API was unavailable at time of survey — no population figures could be confirmed from tool output.

# Locality Guide: Norway (1820–1900)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Country:** Norway (standardPlace: `Norway`)
- **State church:** Church of Norway (Lutheran) — kept primary vital records
- **Naming custom:** Patronymic: men `-sen`, women `-datter` from father's first name; changed each generation; fixed surnames not standard until 1923 Act.

## Available record types

### Church records (kirkebøker) — PRIMARY SOURCE
- Norway, Marriages, 1660–1926 (FS col. 1468080): 1,330,979 indexed records; **0 images** — index only
- Norway, Church Books, 1797–1958 (FS col. 4237104): 14,398,439 records; 1,288,153 images — indexed + images
- Norway, Baptisms, 1634–1927 (FS col. 1467014): 5,277,294 records
- 18,963+ digitized volumes (marriage/religious types) in FamilySearch image archive; most are **0% indexed, browse-only**, in Norwegian
- Also on Digitalarkivet.no (free): https://digitalarkivet.no/

### Civil registration
- Civil Marriage Index 1863–1919 and related sets on Digitalarkivet.no; broader coverage from 1880s–1893 depending on parish.

### Censuses (FamilySearch)
- 1865 (col. 3756102), 1870 (col. 4135961), 1875 (col. 1529106), 1891 (col. 4067726), 1900 (col. 3744863)

### Probate
- Norway, Probate Index Cards, 1640–1903 (col. 1661306): 1,058,029 records

### Migration
- Norway, Emigration Records, 1874–1960 on Ancestry (col. 61757)

## Research tips
- Identify the parish first using the indexed marriage collection, then retrieve images.
- Search censuses (1865, 1875) to place the subject in a specific parish.
- Search Digitalarkivet.no in parallel with FamilySearch.
- Records in Norwegian/Dano-Norwegian; key terms: dato, navn, foreldre.
